subject: Cloudflare
tagline: The connectivity cloud that hosts AI agents: the Agents SDK on Durable Objects, Workers AI inference, AI Gateway and managed MCP servers.

sources.title: Cloudflare: Build for the agent era
Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang (26 October 2026)
Cloudflare Workers AI: Edge AI Inference Platform
Workers AI: serverless GPU-powered inference on Cloudflare's global network (27 September 2023)
Piecing together the Agent puzzle: MCP, authentication & authorization, and Durable Objects free tier (7 April 2025)
Cloudflare's AI Platform: an inference layer designed for agents (16 April 2026)
Agents SDK v0.3.0 with AI SDK v6 (changelog, 22 December 2025)
The impact of the Salesloft Drift breach on Cloudflare and our customers (2 September 2025)

what_it_does.text: Cloudflare runs a global network and security platform, now pitched as one platform for apps, agents and workforce. For agents it offers the Agents SDK, which hosts each agent as a Durable Object with its own storage, scheduling and tools (browser, sandbox, web search, MCP, payments), Workers AI for serverless model inference, and AI Gateway to log, cache, route, rate-limit and budget model calls across providers. It also runs managed remote MCP servers that let outside agents read and change a Cloudflare account through its API.

agents.name: Agents SDK agent
agents.what: An agent a developer builds and Cloudflare hosts: each agent is a Durable Object with a durable identity, local SQL storage, real-time connections, scheduled work and recoverable execution; a harness (Pi, OpenCode or Think) runs the loop that calls models and tools. Reached by chat, voice, email, Slack and webhooks.
actions: Calls Workers AI models, AI Gateway catalog models and vendor models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) through one createAI provider
Connects to external MCP servers with addMcpServer and passes their tools into model calls, with OAuth or bearer tokens
Uses a workspace, a Linux sandbox, web fetch, web search, a browser (Browser Run), AI Search and Code Mode
Pays for resources and tools through x402 and the Machine Payments Protocol
Keeps state in SQL storage, schedules future work, hibernates when idle

agents.name: Cloudflare API MCP
agents.what: Cloudflare's managed remote MCP server at mcp.cloudflare.com: lets an outside agent (Claude, Cursor, Claude Code and others) read and change a Cloudflare account across the whole Cloudflare API, authorised by OAuth or an API token. Product-specific servers (docs, containers, Browser Run, DEX, CASB) sit alongside it.
actions: search() and execute() over more than 2,500 Cloudflare API endpoints (DNS, Workers, R2, Zero Trust and every other product)
Runs model-written JavaScript against the API inside an isolated Dynamic Worker sandbox
docs() to search Cloudflare developer documentation
Reads account configuration, makes suggestions and can make the suggested changes

agents.name: Workers AI inference
agents.what: The serverless inference service agents call: 50+ open-source models (including GLM-5.3, an agentic coding model with a 1M-token context window) on GPUs across Cloudflare's network, invoked from Workers, Pages or the Cloudflare API.
actions: Runs text, image and embedding models for agents through the AI binding or REST API
Processes prompts and returns outputs; documented as zero data retention for standard inference
Serves as the default model for Agents SDK examples

agents.name: AI Gateway
agents.what: The control layer between an agent and its models: one API and binding for Workers AI and 20+ third-party providers, with logging, analytics, caching, rate and spend limits, routing and fallback, guardrails, DLP, stored provider keys and identity through Cloudflare Access.
actions: Routes and retries model calls across providers; holds third-party provider keys or bills through Unified Billing
Logs prompts, responses, tokens and cost (logging on by default)
Blocks requests over a spend limit with HTTP 429; scans prompts and responses with DLP; moderates with guardrails
Buffers streaming responses so an interrupted agent can reconnect

use_cases.name: Aug to Sep 2026: GLM-5.3 answers held other customers' data
use_cases.who: Customers whose applications and agents sent very long prompts to the GLM-5.3 model (@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3) on Workers AI, a model built for agentic coding with a 1M-token context window. Reconstructed from Cloudflare's own report of 26 October 2026.

reach.what: The customer's prompt: very long context sent by an agent or app to GLM-5.3 (affected prompts were longer than 681,280 tokens)
The shared KV cache pool in GPU memory: fixed-size pages reused between requests and not zeroed; the prefill pool held 681,280 tokens against an advertised 1,048,576-token context
Other customers' prompts and partial generations left in stale cache pages from requests made shortly before
Responses delivered to a different customer: 155 responses between 27 August and 9 September 2026, returned with HTTP 200 and coherent text
Where a response is kept afterwards: AI Gateway logs (prompt and response, on by default for each gateway) and the agent's own storage

mandate.what: As documented on the Workers AI data usage page: inputs and outputs are Customer Content, Cloudflare does not make it available to other Cloudflare customers, and standard inference keeps no inputs or outputs after the response
Illustrative: the customer's agent sends its own project context and gets back an answer built only from its own request

gap.what: The model was advertised with a 1,048,576-token context while the cache pool held 681,280 tokens; the mismatch was known before launch and pre-launch tests checked only status codes and performance, not output, so the isolation between customers rested on an untested assumption.

Nothing in the response marked the leak: the client got HTTP 200 and a coherent reply, so another customer's data could flow into an agent's context and into stored logs without either customer seeing it.

controls.what: Vulnerability report through Cloudflare's HackerOne programme; the model was set private (requests return HTTP 400) within 40 minutes of declaring the incident

Configuration fixed so the prefill pool holds about 2.04 million tokens (twice the context); engine patched to retire rejected requests before any KV transfer; fixes upstreamed in SGLang v0.5.20 to v0.5.22
Every disaggregated deployment change now checks KV pool size against context length, deferred release and transfer bounds; per-transfer KV checksums and canaries being extended
AI Gateway DLP can scan model responses as well as prompts and flag or block sensitive data

simulation.action: 27 August 2026: GLM-5.3 launches on Workers AI with a 1,048,576-token context and a 681,280-token prefill pool; the mismatch is known and long-context tests return success codes
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the advertised context and the cache pool disagreeing, and that the evidence for safe handling was status codes, not checked output.

simulation.action: (illustrative) A customer's coding agent sends a prompt of about 700,000 tokens with its project context to @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3
The engine rejects the over-length prompt internally, swaps in a one-token placeholder and still hands off to decode, which attends over reserved pages still holding earlier requests' data
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows other customers' prompts inside this request's reach, against the documented commitment that Customer Content is not made available to other customers.

simulation.action: The reply returns HTTP 200, coherent, containing other users' content; 155 responses are affected between 27 August and 9 September
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows data leaving one customer's boundary for another with no error raised, so neither side had a signal that the mandate was broken.

simulation.action: (illustrative) The receiving agent stores the reply in its conversation state, and the gateway's default logging keeps the prompt and response
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows another customer's content now persisted in this customer's logs and agent storage, outside the zero-retention path.

simulation.action: 8 September, 23:11 UTC: a security researcher reports the leak through HackerOne; 9 September 13:22 incident declared, reproduced with two accounts; 14:00 model set private
9 September: pool resized and engine patched, validated against the researcher's script; model restored at 19:40; 26 October coordinated disclosure, no evidence of deliberate exploitation found

use_cases.name: A coding agent changes a Cloudflare account through MCP
use_cases.who: A developer who connects a coding agent (for example Claude Code or Cursor) to the Cloudflare API MCP server to add a DNS record for one site (an illustrative case built on the documented server).

reach.what: The whole Cloudflare API through two tools: more than 2,500 endpoints across DNS, Workers, R2, Zero Trust and every other product
Model-written JavaScript run against the API client inside an isolated Dynamic Worker sandbox
DNS records and Worker deployments the agent can create or change
Account configuration, logs and analytics the agent can read
Zero Trust and security configuration, reachable through the same API
The grant itself: OAuth permissions chosen at connect, or a user or account API token passed as a bearer token for automation

mandate.what: Illustrative: read the zone's configuration and add one DNS record for one site
Illustrative: no changes to Zero Trust policies, Workers or other zones without the owner's approval

gap.what: One server covers the entire API, so the only boundary is the permissions chosen at OAuth time or on the token; a broad grant puts security policy and every product within reach of a task that needs one record.
Changes are made by code the model writes and runs in one execute() call; the docs describe the agent making suggested changes for you, with no documented per-change approval on this server.

controls.what: OAuth authorization at connect, where the user selects the permissions to grant to the agent; API tokens scoped to the permissions needed
Generated code runs in an isolated Dynamic Worker sandbox
For agents built with Code Mode: connector calls can require approval (requiresApproval, approve, reject) and the runtime records execution, replay and rollback

simulation.action: (illustrative) Connects the coding agent to mcp.cloudflare.com and approves the OAuth permissions it asks for
(illustrative) Uses docs() and search() to find the DNS endpoints
(illustrative) Reads the zone's configuration and recent analytics
(illustrative) Writes and runs code with execute() that creates the DNS record
(illustrative) Judging that an Access policy blocks its test of the new hostname, edits the Zero Trust policy in the same session
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows security policy inside the agent's reach for a DNS task, and that the grant, not the task, set the boundary.

simulation.action: (illustrative) Redeploys a Worker on another zone to "fix" a route it found while testing
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows write access to other zones and Workers under the same token, with no approval step in evidence on the server.

simulation.action: (illustrative) Reviews the changes in the dashboard after the session

use_cases.name: A support agent with tools, a browser and payments
use_cases.who: A company building a customer-support agent on the Agents SDK with a knowledge base, external MCP tools, a browser and paid data services (an illustrative case built on the documented SDK).

reach.what: The agent's own state: SQL storage, chat history and an AI Search knowledge base it can write back to
External MCP servers (for example GitHub), whose tools go into model calls, acting on behalf of the end user with an OAuth grant
A browser that keeps tabs, cookies and login sessions between turns, and can open sites the agent serves itself
Payments: x402 (stablecoins such as USDC) and the Machine Payments Protocol, paid programmatically with no pre-shared key; human approval on the x402 client is optional
A Linux sandbox for shell commands and scripts; it cannot read the agent's storage or bindings and reaches the internet only when allowed
Models from many providers through AI Gateway, which holds the vendor keys or bills through Unified Billing

mandate.what: Illustrative: answer customers from the knowledge base and read issue activity; no actions in customers' own accounts
Illustrative: spend on models and paid services within a monthly budget, and any single payment over a threshold only with a person's approval

gap.what: The browser keeps logins between turns, and MCP tools act with the end user's grant, so the agent can reach into accounts that the support task only needs to read about.
Human approval for x402 payments is optional on the client; unless the developer sets it, the agent can pay a 402 challenge on its own.

controls.what: Dynamic tool approval (needsApproval, for example only for amounts over 100) since Agents SDK v0.3.0
Human-in-the-loop patterns: MCP elicitation, Workflow approvals that can wait months, and Code Mode approvals on connector calls
AI Gateway spend limits by model, provider, user or team, blocking with HTTP 429 when the budget is reached (eventually consistent)
AI Gateway behind Cloudflare Access ties each request to a verified user for logs, analytics and spend
Sandbox isolation from the agent's storage, variables and bindings; internet only when allowed

simulation.action: (illustrative) Answers a customer by calling search_knowledge_base and saves the resolution back
(illustrative) Calls a GitHub MCP tool to summarise the latest issue activity
(illustrative) Reopens a browser tab where a customer's dashboard is still logged in and changes a setting to reproduce the bug
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows a logged-in session in a customer's account within the agent's reach, outside a mandate that allows reading only.

simulation.action: (illustrative) Pays a 402 challenge for a premium data API with no approval configured
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows money reachable without a person's approval, because the approval on the payment client was left optional.

simulation.action: (illustrative) Runs a reproduction script in the sandbox
(illustrative) Calls a frontier model through AI Gateway; the team's spend limit is close and later requests get HTTP 429

incidents.what: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 model on Workers AI: 155 responses to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens contained data from other customers' requests made shortly before. Reported by a security researcher through HackerOne; Cloudflare took the model offline within 40 minutes of declaring an incident, restored it the same day with a corrected configuration and patched engine, and found no evidence of deliberate exploitation.

Salesloft Drift breach: a threat actor used OAuth credentials of the Drift chat agent's Salesforce integration to exfiltrate support case text from Cloudflare's Salesforce tenant (12 to 17 August 2025). Cloudflare found 104 Cloudflare API tokens in the data and rotated them, disconnected all third-party integrations from Salesforce, and said no Cloudflare services or infrastructure were compromised.

leads.claim: Workers AI runs AI models serverlessly on Cloudflare's network, from Workers, Pages or the Cloudflare API, without managing infrastructure.
AI Gateway is a control layer providing visibility, routing, billing, caching and security, working with Workers AI and other providers.
leads.note: The overview page (s4) lists analytics, logging, caching, rate limiting and routing; billing and security controls are named in the changelog.

leads.claim: Developers build agents on Cloudflare with Workers AI and the Agents SDK.
AI Gateway routes requests to Workers AI and third-party models, with observability and caching.
Use case: customer support and task automation agents reaching Workers AI, Workers, Pages and the Cloudflare API (cited the Workers AI page).

leads.claim: Use case: managed routing across Workers AI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenAI and Replicate, with logs, billing and API keys.

leads.claim: Coding agents and non-browser clients can call an Access-protected gateway by sending the Access token as a bearer token.

Workers AI requests through AI Gateway require the cf-aig-gateway-id header.
AI Gateway supports Workers AI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenAI and Replicate.
AI Search instances connect to an AI Gateway; embedding, reranking, query rewriting and response generation can run through it.
leads.note: Workers AI embedding and reranking are included in AI Search and do not appear in gateway logs.

The Workers docs highlight serverless AI inference for running LLMs and generating images with Workers AI.

AI Gateway is a front door to models with routing, caching, rate and spend controls and observability.
Agents integrate with tools and data through MCP.
Agent instances run on Durable Objects using the Agents SDK.
Agents invoke models through Workers AI and/or AI Gateway model providers in the Agents SDK.
Managed remote MCP servers let an agent search documentation, call the Cloudflare API and query logs and analytics.

Workers AI serves inference globally with one API call.

AI Gateway caches identical requests in Cloudflare's global cache.
AI Gateway enforces rate limits and spend limits.
AI Gateway can be protected with Cloudflare Access so the authenticated identity is used in logs, analytics, routing and spend controls.

MCP servers can request input from the client during tool calls (elicitation).
Durable state and persistence are described in Cloudflare MCP server one-pager materials.

leads.claim: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model gave some customers data from other customers' requests between 27 August and 9 September 2026; the model was offline within 40 minutes of declaring an incident.
Agents such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Claude Code can answer questions about Cloudflare products, generate configuration and call Cloudflare APIs on a user's behalf.

leads.note: Read on the Agents overview, not the cited MCP page.

leads.note: Read on the Agents overview, not the cited MCP page.

leads.claim: The Cloudflare API MCP server searches and executes calls across over 2,500 endpoints (DNS, Workers, R2, Zero Trust and others).
The Cloudflare API MCP server searches Cloudflare developer documentation.
It generates and runs JavaScript against the API inside an isolated Dynamic Worker sandbox.
It can make suggested configuration changes, within the permissions granted during OAuth authorization.
An AI Search example agent creates its own instance, indexes documents, calls search_knowledge_base and stores chat history in a Durable Object.
Knock uses the Agents SDK to build and ship its remote MCP server (Cloudflare testimonial).

The blog gives email, meeting booking and code deployment as examples of such actions.

Global outage on 18 November 2025 caused by a bug generating a Bot Management feature file.
Outage on 5 December 2025 of about 25 minutes from configuration changes to mitigate a React Server Components vulnerability; not an attack.
Attackers exploited the Salesloft Drift chat agent's Salesforce integration to access Salesforce tenants of Cloudflare and others (date not given).

leads.note: The StatusGator page read today lists only recent incidents (October and November 2026).

AI Gateway offers caching, rate limiting, fallback routing and request logs covering prompt, response, provider, token usage and cost.
leads.note: Features on the overview (s4); log fields on the logging page.

leads.claim: AI Gateway is a unified inference layer for models from 14+ providers through the same binding as Workers AI.
leads.note: The post says 70+ models across 12+ providers.

leads.claim: AI Gateway buffers streaming responses independently of the agent's lifetime, so an interrupted agent can reconnect without paying twice.
Agents SDK v0.3.0 (December 2025) added dynamic tool approval for human-in-the-loop and a unified server-side tool pattern.
Agents hibernate when idle and wake on demand; each is a persistent stateful environment on Durable Objects.
Managed remote MCP servers are reached with OAuth; API tokens can be used for CI/CD or automation.
Workers AI is billed on usage, and Workers charges CPU time rather than wall time waiting on I/O.
Cloudflare states the outages of 5 December 2025 and 20 February 2026 were not caused by attacks.
leads.note: The 5 December statement is on the outage list (s25).

questions: After the GLM-5.3 exposure, what tells a Workers AI customer, per request, that the answer was built only from its own data, and were the customers who received or supplied the 155 affected responses told which requests were involved?
Can a Cloudflare API MCP server session be limited to one zone and read-only by default, with each write held for a person's approval, rather than relying on the OAuth scopes chosen at connect?
Is every action an agent takes through the MCP server recorded in the account audit log as that agent, separately from the human who granted it?
For agents that pay through x402 or MPP, can an account set a hard spending ceiling and mandatory approval that the developer cannot leave optional?
Browser sessions keep cookies and logins between turns: which controls stop an agent from using a logged-in session for something its task did not need, and is that use logged?
